subject: Technical supplement: RM-Enterprise RFP — SDLC & Vulnerability Management deliverables
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita.rao@evergreenbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RM-Enterprise RFP — request for technical supplement (SDLC / VM / SBOM)

Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for taking our RFP — a few of our internal risk reviewers asked for a short technical supplement that pulls together your SDLC controls, vulnerability management posture (SAST/DAST cadence, pen test history, patch SLAs) and a bill-of-materials (SBOM) snapshot for the services we'll be onboarding.

Can you provide: 
- a concise SDLC summary (code review, dependency scans, release gating)
- most recent pen test executive summary (Q2 2026 if available)
- SAST/DAST cadence and toolset, with evidence artifacts or report IDs
- patching SLA matrix for CVEs by severity and typical turnaround
- SBOM inventory for inference runtime and the web console (CSV OK)

We'd like the supplement by EOD 2026-07-15 to meet our procurement window. I'm copying Tom (Ops) for any environment-specific questions.

Thanks,
Anita Rao
Head of Vendor Security - Evergreen Bank
attachments: evergreen_rfp_questions_v3.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita.rao@evergreenbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RM-Enterprise RFP — request for technical supplement (SDLC / VM / SBOM)

Hi Anita — thanks for the note and clear checklist. We'll assemble a focused technical appendix that addresses each bullet. Quick plan: 
- I'll own the SDLC and release-gating summary and produce a 1-page control map.
- Neha will provide SAST/DAST, pen test summaries, and evidence pointers.
- Marissa will extract the SBOM inventory for the requested runtime images and console components.
- We'll include a patch-SLA table and example JIRA/issue IDs showing typical remediation timelines.

One quick clarification: for SBOM scope, do you need transitive dependency lists for both the inference runtime (GPU-serving containers) and the control-plane web console? We can provide both, but the runtime SBOM will include GPU-optimized libraries that are large.

We intend to deliver the appendix plus the artifacts as a zipped packet and provide a short readout call if you'd like. Target: 2026-07-15 EOD as requested.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: DRAFT: Technical appendix sections (SAST/DAST, pen tests, patch SLAs)

Karthik / Marissa — attaching draft pieces I've pulled together for the appendix. Key points included: 
- SAST: run weekly (Snyk + internal linters), PR gating for high/critical findings, triage board with SLA.
- DAST: quarterly external scans with authenticated flows; dynamic scans for console + API endpoints; automated nightly smoke scans.
- Pen tests: Q2 2026 external test (red-team vendor: ColdHammer Security) — low/medium findings remediated; executive summary attached.
- Patch SLAs: critical (CVSS >=9.0) — 48 hours to mitigation plan, 7 days to patch deployment; high (7.0-8.9) — 7–14 days; medium — 30 days. Exceptions: coordinated maintenance windows for customer-dedicated deployments.

Attachments (drafts): rdw_pentest-summary-q2-2026.pdf (exec summary), patch-sla-matrix.csv (proposed SLA table).

I'll mark any internal-only notes in the document and remove before sending externally. Let me know if you want the CVE-to-ticket mapping included in the packet or as a separate evidence binder.

-Neha
Security Lead, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Beckett <t.beckett@evergreenbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita.rao@evergreenbank.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RM-Enterprise RFP — request for technical supplement (SDLC / VM / SBOM)

Thanks — quick follow-up on patch SLAs. Our procurement team wants a sample runbook describing how you triage and patch a new critical CVE that impacts a shared open-source library used by the inference runtime. Specifically: 
- confirmation you can map a CVE to affected images and customers,
- typical lead time to publish a patched image, and
- whether you support hotfixes for Dedicated/Private customers outside scheduled maintenance.

Also, for the SBOM CSV: can you include package origin (public registry vs. internal fork) and license fields? That helps our legal/compliance quick scan.

Appreciate it — if you can answer in the packet or call this week that would be great.

—Tom
Director, Cloud Ops — Evergreen Bank
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita.rao@evergreenbank.com>, Tom Beckett <t.beckett@evergreenbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RM-Enterprise RFP — request for technical supplement (SDLC / VM / SBOM)

Anita / Tom — attached is the requested technical appendix and evidence packet. Highlights and answers inline: 

1) SDLC and release-gating (technical-appendix-sdlc-vm.docx)
- PR gating: failing SAST rules for critical/high blocks merge; code owners enforced.
- CI: dependency scans on merge; SBOM generated per image build.

2) SAST / DAST / Pen test (rdw_pentest-summary-q2-2026.pdf)
- SAST cadence: weekly Snyk scans + pre-merge linters.
- DAST cadence: quarterly authenticated scans for console + API; nightly lightweight checks.
- Pen test: ColdHammer exec summary attached; all medium findings closed or mitigated with tickets (see ticket refs in appendix).

3) Patch SLA & runbook (patch-sla-matrix.csv + runbook excerpt below)
- Detection & mapping: automated CVE ingestion maps to images via SBOM hashes and container image metadata; internal tooling flags affected customers within 2 hours of vendor advisory ingestion.
- Patch timeline (standard): 48h to mitigation plan for critical; 7 days to patched image where possible. Patch images published to our registry and staged to Dedicated pools; canaries run for 2–6 hours depending on image size.
- Hotfix support: for Dedicated and Private customers we offer expedited hotfix windows outside scheduled maintenance under our incident playbook (requires support ticket and, for Private, customer approval for the patch window).

Runbook excerpt (summary):
- T+0: CVE received → triage (auto-match to SBOM hashes) → severity confirmed; customers affected enumerated.
- T+2h: mitigation plan (temporary config or WAF rule) + ticket created + customer notif.
- T+48h: patched image build + QA smoke.
- T+72h–7d: staged rollout (canary → full pool) depending on image size and risk.

4) SBOM (redwood_sbom_inventory_20260712.csv)
- CSV includes package, version, package-origin (registry vs internal-fork), license. We include transitive dependencies for runtime images; file size noted in appendix.

Attachments included in zip: technical-appendix-sdlc-vm.docx, redwood_sbom_inventory_20260712.csv, rdw_pentest-summary-q2-2026.pdf, patch-sla-matrix.csv.

If helpful I can schedule a 30-minute readout later this week to walk through the runbook and the SBOM fields.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
attachments: technical-appendix-sdlc-vm.docx; redwood_sbom_inventory_20260712.csv; rdw_pentest-summary-q2-2026.pdf; patch-sla-matrix.csv
